question.text:
Unit vectors u, v satisfy u · v = 1/2. What is v · [u × (u × v)]?
(A) −1 (B) −3/4 (C) −1/2 (D) 0 (E) 3/4

solution.text:
The vector triple-product identity gives u × (u × v) = u(u · v) − v(u · u) = u/2 − v. Dotting
with v gives 1/4 − 1 = −3/4. Replacing the nested cross product by (u × u) × v = 0 would
incorrectly assume associativity.

question.text:

question.text:
Let R(x, y, z) = (−x, y, z), reflection in the yz-plane. If u × v = (1, 2, 3), what is (Ru) × (Rv)?
(A) (−1, 2, 3)
(B) (1, 2, 3)
(C) (1, −2, −3)
(D) (−1, −2, −3)
(E) It cannot be determined.

solution.text:
Writing the cross product in components shows that reflection of the inputs preserves
its first component and reverses the other two. Equivalently, an orientation-reversing
orthogonal map satisfies (Ru) × (Rv) = −R(u × v). The result is (1, −2, −3).
